instruction: Open the provided init.ifc model in Bonsai and use init_plan.png as the plan reference. Consolidate duplicate element types and material assignments so each repeated construction or product family uses a single shared IFC type. Save the completed IFC4 model as result.ifc and export a type and material occurrence schedule as result.csv using a Bonsai or IfcCSV-style workflow. The result should keep one project, one site, one building, and one building storey, and it should contain no building element proxies or furniture. Model exactly four walls assigned by one IfcRelDefinesByType relationship to one IfcWallType named WallType_External with material layer summary Brick:0.100m | Insulation:0.050m | Gypsum:0.015m. Model exactly one slab assigned to one IfcSlabType named SlabType_200 with material summary Concrete:0.200m. Model exactly two doors assigned to one IfcDoorType named Door Type A with material Timber. Model exactly four windows assigned to one IfcWindowType named Window Type W with material Aluminum. The IFC file should contain exactly six IfcMaterial objects named Brick, Insulation, Gypsum, Concrete, Timber, and Aluminum. The CSV should have headers Class, TypeName, MaterialSummary, and OccurrenceCount, with exactly four rows: IfcWall / WallType_External / Brick:0.100m | Insulation:0.050m | Gypsum:0.015m / 4; IfcSlab / SlabType_200 / Concrete:0.200m / 1; IfcDoor / Door Type A / Timber / 2; and IfcWindow / Window Type W / Aluminum / 4. Other details may vary.
